newsitem.title: USA: Salix says Colazide effective in Phase III tests.
newsitem.headline: Salix says Colazide effective in Phase III tests.

text.p: Salix Holdings Ltd said results of its Phase III trial of Colazide, used to treat ulcerative colitis, showed the drug had greater efficacy and a better safety profile than mesalazine, a current treatment for acute ulcerative colitis.
Shares of Palo Alto-based Salix are traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the name SLX.S, a company spokesman said.

In the study Colazide, which is balsalazide disodium, showed a mean time of 10 days until the first symptom-free day for sufferers of ulcerative colitis. That compares to 25 days for patients using mesalazine.
The results of the study were presented at the recent annual meeting of the British Society of Gastroenterology by Jonathan R.B. Green, the principal investigator for the study, the company said.
The study was sponsored by Astra AB, Salix's marketing partner for Colazide in northern Europe, North America and throughout most of the world.

Ulcerative colitis is a form of inflammatory bowel disease and is characterized by chronic inflamation of the intestinal mucosa in the colon, with symptoms including diarrhea, abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and fever.
